diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17: lineids 4C:D7:C8:93:BA:F1 and 4C:D7:C8:7F:0A:B9. Only one ONU can occupy that slot, creating a provisioning and identity conflict. The currently observed ONU is online and passing traffic, so there is no present optical or access outage.
evidence: The duplicate_onu_slot check directly reports two active CRM records mapped to EPON0/4:17, which is an impossible one-slot/two-ONU assignment.
The subscriber is currently online, responds to SNMP, completes authentication, and has normal optical readings: RX about -20.91 dBm and TX about 2.38 dBm.
The seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable within the healthy noise range; distance is constant at 134, bias current is stable around 11 mA, and there is no fibre or laser degradation.
All tested ONUs on EPON0/4 are online, so there is no ONU-offline, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has healthy CPU, memory, and temperature, and all eight PONs are reported healthy; the OLT and router are not at fault.
The OLT offline count is 14 of 272 customers, consistent with the approximately 4.85% network baseline and not evidence of an outage.
Authentication is consistent with an existing RADIUS entry, only two sessions occurred in 24 hours, average duration is about 11.8 hours, and the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1044.
The direct duplicate slot evidence is therefore the only abnormality and affects two customer records sharing one physical slot.

remediation.action: Verify the physical ONU identity at EPON0/4:17, determine which CRM record is valid, and remove or deactivate the stale duplicate record. Correct any incorrect slot or lineid assignment, then reconcile the OLT configuration, CRM, and RADIUS records. Re-run the ONU discovery and duplicate-slot checks after the correction, avoiding disruption to the currently valid subscriber.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
